title: SSA produces no φ-functions or def-use edges for any input; the SSA tests check only counts and CSR shape
evidence: Variable identity is the AST node index: liveness.rs:134-135 does `let sym_id = node; defs.push(sym_id)`, while uses push identifier-node ids (139-141, 159-160). Phase5Stage ignores `_sta` (ssa/mod.rs:34). A def node never equals a use node, so placement.rs:45 `is_live_in(y, var_sym)` is never true (no φ), and renaming.rs:150 `vstack.top(u)` never hits (empty def-use). points_to.rs:31 and object_diagram.rs:16 then call `sta.symbol(orig_sym_id)` on that node index. ssa_tests.rs:84-92 and pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:179-202 assert only counts and CSR shape; the uniqueness check holds by construction.
impact: Phase 5 output (φ, def-use, versions) is empty or meaningless for every program, which corrupts points-to, slicing, DFG and object diagrams. Deleting φ placement entirely would still pass the whole suite.
recommendation: Key SSA on resolved symbol ids, and introduce newtypes (NodeId, SymId, SsaId) so this ID-space confusion fails to compile. Add oracle tests: `int x=0; if(c) x=1; return x;` must yield exactly one φ(x) at the join, with two args, and the return's use must chain to it. A loop counter must get versions 0..2. Add proptest over generated structured programs asserting every use is dominated by its unique reaching def (Cytron et al. 1991). The φ count must equal a naive iterated-dominance-frontier reference keyed by symbol.

title: Call resolution returns the enclosing method, so the call graph is mostly self-loops; no test asserts a single edge
evidence: resolve_method_target (resolution.rs:179-238) never matches by name. Step 1 needs def_node == call_node. Step 3 needs a method whose first_token_id equals the call-site token, but method symbols take their declaration's first token (pass1_discovery.rs:178). Step 4 returns the first method whose token range encloses the call, which is the caller. Edges become (caller, caller) (cg/mod.rs:87-93), and Tarjan classifies nearly every calling method SELF_RECURSIVE (scc.rs:40-48). cg_tests.rs:79-87 asserts method_count>0, non-empty SCCs and round-trip counts; the surgical dump (575-626) only range-checks ids.
impact: Call edges, recursion classes, PSA unwind depths, CFL reachability, slicing and sequence/communication diagrams are wrong for ordinary code. Dropping or reversing every edge would also pass the suite.
recommendation: Add golden edge-set tests: for the cg_tests fixture, assert edges == {main→<init>, main→helper, main→recurse, recurse→recurse}, with SCC class SELF only for recurse. Add a property: a self-edge exists only if the body syntactically calls its own name with matching arity. Add a nightly differential job on pinned repos comparing against a CHA call graph from SootUp or WALA (or the JavaParser symbol solver), with edge precision/recall thresholds that fail CI.

title: Phase 8 longest-path DFS enumerates every CFG path: exponential hang on ordinary methods
evidence: psa/construction/mod.rs:153-173 compute_max_path_length pops (block, depth) and pushes every successor with depth+1 (line 168), with no visited or memo set. The only cut is depth >= bound, where bound = block count (158), and acyclic paths never reach it. It runs for every function (mod.rs:116, via psa/mod.rs:129). A Python model of if_stmt.rs block shapes (scratchpad lens/scale_model.py) costs exactly 4·2^k pops for k sequential ifs: k=22 gives 16.8M pops and k=40 gives 4.4·10^12. Loops turn it into walk enumeration up to length n.
impact: Any method with roughly 35+ independent branches (serializers, toXContent, validators) never finishes Phase 8, so the CLI run and the server request hang. Remotely triggerable through POST /api/analyze.
recommendation: Replace the DFS with DAG dynamic programming. Drop the back edges already found by analyze_loops, iterate blocks in RPO, and compute len[v] = 1 + max(len[p]) in O(B+E). Count paths the same way (cnt[v] = Σcnt[p], saturating or log2/BigUint) instead of relying on #SAT for metrics. Add a 64-sequential-if regression test with a 1 s budget, and a per-function work budget for any remaining enumeration.

title: Call resolution returns the caller itself; the error cascades into SCCs, PSA, entry points, sequence diagrams and queries
evidence: resolve_method_target never compares names. Step 3 matches a declaration's first token, which is never a call token. Step 4 returns the first method whose token span encloses the call, i.e. the caller (resolution.rs:179-238). For `t.helper()` the 'name' token picked is the receiver `t` (call_sites.rs:153-163). Self-edges are kept (cg/mod.rs:88-91,114-127), so every method that makes a call becomes SELF_RECURSIVE (scc.rs:40-47) and loses entry-point status (actor_identification.rs:18-43). call_block is always 0 because blocks hold statements, not call nodes (call_sites.rs:142-151). Field-initializer calls are dropped (call_sites.rs:32-35). cg_tests.rs:79-87 checks only counts.
impact: Every call edge is a self-loop or an override of the caller. The call graph, recursion flags, PSA unwinding, entry points, sequence and communication diagrams, slices, impact sets and reachability queries are therefore wrong for all input.
recommendation: Resolve callees by (name_id, arity, receiver static type), using Phase 3 scopes and the receiver's type_id. Then expand with CHA (Dean et al., ECOOP'95) or RTA (Bacon-Sweeney, OOPSLA'96) over th_edges. Record call_block through a statement-to-block map built in Phase 4. Done = the cg_tests fixture yields exactly main->helper, main->recurse and recurse->recurse. Then score against the CATS/Judge suites (Reif et al., ISSTA'18/'19) and diff against Soot or OPAL output.

title: Kotlin and every non-Java language are parsed by different grammars in different phases; Phase 3 covers this with a raw-token keyword sweep
evidence: Phase 1 parses .kt files with tree_sitter_java (ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31). Phase 2 has no Kotlin adapter and falls back to the JavaScript grammar (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28,41). Python, Rust, TS, C++ and Go use the JavaScript grammar in both phases (ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:29-39,56). Phase 2 then maps JS-grammar nodes onto Java-grammar tokens by (line, col). Phase 3 always uses JavaSemanticAdapter (symbol/mod.rs:38), plus a keyword sweep over raw tokens (pass1_discovery.rs:200-460). Symbols from the sweep have no decl_node, so Phase 4 skips them (cfg/mod.rs:55-58). The sweep turns `var`/`val` locals into SK_FIELDs (pass1_discovery.rs:414-450) and never resets current_class_sym per file (pass1_discovery.rs:257).
impact: Kotlin functions found by the sweep get no CFG, SSA, call edges or activity diagram. Kotlin and Java 10+ local variables appear as class fields. Top-level Kotlin functions attach to a class in another file. The multi-language claims rest on keyword heuristics.
recommendation: Create one LanguageRegistry (grammar, CST reducer, semantic adapter) keyed by LangId and used by Phases 1-3. Add pinned tree-sitter-kotlin and the other grammars, or reject unsupported extensions with a diagnostic. Remove the token sweep once Kotlin reduction exists. Per-language golden fixtures must assert classes, members and per-function CFG counts, plus a test that no SK_FIELD symbol lies inside a method body.

title: Exponential path enumeration in compute_max_path_length makes Phase 8 hang on common methods
evidence: compute_max_path_length (psa/construction/mod.rs:153-173) is a DFS with no visited set and no memo. It pushes every successor with depth+1 until depth >= block count, so it enumerates every path, and build() calls it for every function (line 116). k sequential `if (c) x++;` statements give 2^k paths, because if_stmt.rs:30-72 builds cond->then->join plus cond->join. A port of the loop counts 5.2M stack pops at k=20 and about 5.5e12 at k=40. Protobuf-generated mergeFrom/writeTo methods, with one `if (hasX())` per field, hit this routinely, and so do loops whose bodies branch.
impact: Phase 8 does not terminate on ordinary large methods. The CLI hangs, and a single POST to the single-threaded server stops it from serving anyone.
recommendation: Compute the longest acyclic path in O(B+E): remove back edges (analyze_loops already finds them), order the resulting DAG topologically and relax each edge once; report loops through unwind_depth. Give every per-function analysis a step budget, in the style of CUDD's node and time limits, that degrades to 'unknown' with a diagnostic. Add regression tests: 64 sequential ifs, and a loop with 10 inner branches, must each finish in under 100 ms.

title: Language-neutral, compiler-grade rewiring of your paths (no hard-coding, no templates)
evidence: OpenHeart must support every language with language-agnostic algorithms, and must never hard-code, template or guess: it works the way compilers do, statically. New code is being written now (read what exists): src/lang (neutral.rs universal vocabulary, frontend.rs LanguageFrontend trait, registry.rs single list of languages, profile.rs, build/ for compile_commands, CMake and MSBuild, preprocess.rs, project_model.rs, uml_semantics.rs, idioms.rs, frontends java, kotlin, c, cpp, csharp); src/ir (typed three-address SSA IR with explicit memory operations, lowering from the AST, dominators); src/memory (abstract heap, field-sensitive points-to with on-the-fly call graph, escape, ownership, mod/ref); src/analysis (lattices, worklist solvers, SCCP, intervals, nullness, typestate, control dependence, IFDS/IDE, contexts, canonical branch conditions); src/derive (every diagram derived from those facts with provenance and a Derivation tag, NotDerivable instead of invention); src/symex (bounded static symbolic execution with a stack, heap and path-condition model producing execution traces); src/abi (C/C++ Itanium and MSVC, JVM and CLR memory layouts, lifetimes, calling conventions); src/arch (architecture recovery: dependency graph, DSM, layers, clustering, metrics, boundaries); src/memview (lifetime, ownership, heap-shape and stack-frame views plus memory-safety and data-race facts). Everything from the architectural flow down to memory-level execution must come from these facts, for every language, with semantics exactly per each language specification. Contract names: LangId::C, LangId::Cpp, LangId::CSharp; ASTNodeType additions NN_NAMESPACE_DECL, NN_STRUCT_DECL, NN_UNION_DECL, NN_TYPEDEF_DECL, NN_FUNCTION_DECL, NN_DESTRUCTOR_DECL, NN_OPERATOR_DECL, NN_TEMPLATE_DECL, NN_PROPERTY_DECL, NN_INDEXER_DECL, NN_EVENT_DECL, NN_DELEGATE_DECL, NN_USING_DIRECTIVE, NN_INCLUDE_DIRECTIVE, NN_GOTO_STMT, NN_LABELED_STMT, NN_FOREACH_STMT, NN_USING_STMT, NN_LOCK_STMT, NN_YIELD_STMT.
impact: Without this, OpenHeart stays Java-specific and heuristic instead of a universal, compiler-grade engine.
recommendation: Rebuild CFG, SSA, CDG and call graph on the new core: CFG and SSA from src/ir (dominators from src/ir/dom.rs), def-use and control dependence from src/analysis, call graph and points-to from src/memory, IFDS from src/analysis/ifds.rs; keep the existing artifact formats as serializations of those results; no Java-specific node names in algorithms.

evidence: The Java reduction table ends with `_ => Drop` (java.rs:129), and Drop discards the whole subtree (reducer.rs:17). constructor_body is unmapped, as are try_with_resources_statement, switch_rule, explicit_constructor_invocation, generic_type, array_type and enum_constant. CFG construction needs an NN_BLOCK child (cfg/mod.rs:59-74), so every constructor gets no CFG, SSA or activity record, and its calls (super(...), new) disappear. pipeline_accuracy_tests.rs:142 asserts function_count == 2 for fixtures with three bodies (OrderService constructor, processOrder, execute), which pins the bug.

title: Phases 3-9 ignore the stored language and hardcode JVM semantics for every file
evidence: The language id is read only in Phases 1-2 (src/ingestion/mod.rs:112; src/ast/mod.rs:73,141). Phase 3 always uses JavaSemanticAdapter (src/symbol/mod.rs:38) and loads only Java stubs (src/symbol/builder.rs:45; java_stubs.rs:119). The symbol model is the JVM's: SymbolVisibility{Package=0,...} (src/core/types/symbol.rs:79-80), STRICTFP and BRIDGE flags (:65,70), and a package-private default for types (src/symbol/adapter/java.rs:125-133). Call kinds mirror invokestatic/invokespecial/invokevirtual (src/cg/call_sites.rs:93-122). Allocation is recognized only as NN_NEW_EXPR (src/cg/points_to.rs:30; associations.rs:98). In src/symbol/uml_meta/associations.rs:40, stubs.contains_key("List") is always true, so every association saved in .sta is an Aggregation (the exporters ignore these records and re-join by name).
impact: Visibility, dispatch, points-to, composition and entry points are wrong or empty for non-JVM languages, and partly for Kotlin, which has no `new`. The dispatch model cannot express C++ non-virtual calls or Rust static dispatch.
recommendation: Store a lang_id on every symbol (SymbolRecord._reserved) and add a per-language LanguageSemantics profile. It covers: a visibility model mapped to UML (internal, pub(crate), fileprivate) with defaults; a dispatch policy (Joern-style STATIC/DYNAMIC plus receiver-type recovery); an allocation recognizer (a call whose callee resolves to a type); the exception model; collection types; entry points; and data-driven stubs (JDK ct.sym, typeshed, lib.d.ts). Fix associations.rs:40 to test the field's own type.

title: The generic adapter is unsound even for JavaScript, the only other real grammar
evidence: src/ingestion/adapter/generic.rs never overrides include_anonymous (default false, src/ingestion/adapter/mod.rs:14-16). As a result, src/ingestion/walker.rs:42 drops every anonymous leaf: '(', '{', ';', '=', 'class', 'import'. Pass 1 names a method by the last identifier before '(', '{' or ';' within 16 tokens (src/symbol/passes/pass1_discovery.rs:696-745), so JS methods and fields get a body identifier as their name. src/ast/adapter/generic.rs has no identifier or type_identifier arm, so there is no NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR or NN_TYPE_REF; SSA uses (src/ssa/liveness.rs:139-161), type refs and call names are all empty. Kinds are matched by substring (:107-116) without an is_named() check, so the anonymous 'class' and 'function' keywords (:35,50) likely create nested duplicate declarations. encode_attrs returns 0 (:120-121), and a println! runs in the hot path (:26-28).
impact: JavaScript class diagrams show wrong member names and probably duplicate classes. The JS data-flow graph, call graph and type relations are empty or point back at the caller. TypeScript, Python and Rust inherit all of this through the fallback.
recommendation: Retire the generic adapter. Give each language an explicit lowering keyed on tree-sitter field names (child_by_field_name: name, body, condition, parameters, superclass) that classifies only named nodes; take names from the name field, not from token scans. Generate exhaustive match tables from each grammar's node-types.json and fail CI on any unmapped named kind. Remove the println!.

title: Empty then/else and loop bodies become dead ends that the builder wires to EXIT
evidence: Each builder connects a branch or body to its join, update block or header only if current_block moved or the entry block has statements. For `if (c) {}`, `while (c) {}` or `for (n = head; n.next != null; n = n.next) {}` the entry block keeps no successor, so the sink loop adds an edge to EXIT. `if (c) {} else { return; }` leaves the join unreachable, and all later code is pruned.
impact: The true branch of an empty body appears to leave the method, loops lose their back edge, and following code can vanish.
recommendation: Always connect the final block of a branch or body, even when empty, to the join, update block or header, and delete the emptiness heuristic. This is separate from FLOW-01, which covers the try/do-while pending-edge path.

title: Def extraction ignores ++/--, compound and chained assignments, and multi-declarator lists
evidence: update_expression maps to NN_UNARY_EXPR and reaches the default branch, so `i++` is only a use. NN_ASSIGN_EXPR pushes the LHS as a def without checking the operator, so `s += i` misses the read of s. `a = b = 0` never visits the inner assignment. `int a = 1, b = 2;` yields one def. `o.f = v` and `a[i] = v` define the access node itself.
impact: Loop counters and accumulators are never redefined, so φs at loop headers cannot appear even after FLOW-04's keying is fixed.
recommendation: Walk expressions recursively in evaluation order. Treat ++/-- and compound assignment as a use plus a def, recurse into nested assignments, emit one def per variable_declarator, and model stores as heap writes plus uses of the base and index. This differs from FLOW-04, which is about identity keying.

title: Use extraction stops one operand deep and skips declaration initializers
evidence: For NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL only direct NN_IDENTIFIER_EXPR children count, but the initializer sits under the nested variable_declarator, so `int y = a + b;` records no uses. For assignments and binaries, operands are pushed as raw nodes without recursion: `x = foo(a)` and `(a + b) * c` record the call or binary node id as a variable and miss a and b.
impact: Most real uses are never seen, so liveness, pruned φ placement and def-use chains stay empty even after keying is fixed.
recommendation: Recurse into every operand subtree and declarator initializer, and emit uses only for identifiers that resolve to variables. Add unit tests for each expression shape. This differs from FLOW-04 (identity) and FLOW-16 (granularity).

title: No entry definitions for parameters, this, captured variables or fields
evidence: Parameters are NN_PARAM_DECL children of the declaration and are never placed in a block. ENTRY is empty, and rename_dfs starts from an empty VersionStack. Uses with no reaching def are silently dropped (`current_ver != u32::MAX`), and φ args get u32::MAX. SSA_FLAG_IS_PARAM_DEF, IS_FIELD_DEF, IS_RETURN_VAL and IS_CONST are never set anywhere.
impact: Parameter-to-use flows, which taint and null analyses need, cannot exist even after FLOW-04 is fixed.
recommendation: Emit version-0 defs in ENTRY for each parameter, `this` and captured variables (optionally fields too), with the flags set. Use an explicit undefined version instead of u32::MAX, and count undefined uses.

title: The BP AST stores no child roles, so consumers decode children by position and misread for and enhanced-for loops
evidence: PreorderArrays hold only type, attr, range and parent. Tree-sitter field names are discarded and NN_ELSE_CLAUSE is never emitted. `for (String s : list) {...}` yields [TYPE_REF, s, list, BLOCK], yet for_stmt.rs:88-101 takes the third child (`list`) as the body. In for_stmt.rs:26-35, `for (; i<n; i++)` and two-variable inits shift the init/cond/update/body positions.
impact: CFGs for common loops lose the real loop body or treat updates as conditions. A dropped then-branch moves the else branch into the then position.
recommendation: Persist a per-node role byte (the tree-sitter field id) in PreorderArrays and in the .bpa. Emit NN_ELSE_CLAUSE or placeholder nodes for omitted parts, and expose child_by_role accessors for the CFG builders.
